# Churchill Downs Closing Week Update: Leading Change Tabbed as 5-2 Morning Line Favorite in Friday's $700,000 Clark presented by Norton Healthcare


## Nov 25, 2026


Wathnan Racing’s unbeaten Travers (GI) winner Leading Change is the 5-2 morning line favorite for Friday’s $700,000 Clark presented by Norton Healthcare (GII) at Churchill Downs where he will face older horses for the first time.


The Brad Cox-trained son of Gun Runner won his June 7 debut at Churchill Downs by 6 ½ lengths and scored by a neck in the $300,000 Indiana Derby (GIII) on July 11 at Horseshoe Indianapolis. In the $1.25 million Travers at Saratoga on Aug. 29, Leading Change ran down Preakness (GI) winner Napoleon Solo to win by a half-length with Kentucky Derby and Belmont Stakes winner Golden Tempo third.


“He’s shown us a lot of talent in three starts,” Cox said. “We knew the Travers would be a tough race to win. The way he ran in the Indiana Derby told us he deserved a shot, and he went up there and beat some very good 3-year-olds. With him being so lightly raced, we’re looking forward to not only Friday’s race but the future as a 4-year-old.”


Manny Franco, who rode Leading Change in the Travers, retains the mount and will break from post No. 2.


Cox also entered Juddmonte’s Dragoon Guard, a 5-year-old son of Arrogate who scored a 3 ¼-length victory in the $500,000 Lukas Classic (GII) on Sept. 26 at Churchill Downs. Tyler Gaffalione rides from post 5.


First post for Friday’s 12-race card is 1 p.m. (all times Eastern) with the 1 1/8-mile Clark scheduled as Race 11 at 5:54 p.m.


The lineup for the Clark from the rail out (with jockey and trainer):


Sir Greylind (Walter Rodriguez, Michel Douaihy, 50-1)
Leading Change (Franco, Cox, 5-2)
Who Dey (Brian Hernandez Jr., Tom Drury Jr., 20-1)
Iron Dome (Flavien Prat, Steve Asmussen, 15-1)
Dragoon Guard (Gaffalione, Cox, 4-1)
This Is Uscar (Edgar Morales, Jordan Blair, 15-1)
Caldera (Jose Ortiz, Saffie Joseph Jr., 8-1)
Willy D’s (John Velazquez, Mike Maker, 6-1)
Bracket Buster (Junior Alvarado, Vicki Oliver, 5-1)
Chunk of Gold (Jaime Torres, Ethan West, 10-1)
Original Sin (Luis Saez, Brendan Walsh, 12-1)
Trainer Ethan West reported Chunk of Gold will likely scratch from Friday’s race to give the colt a little more time between last month’s Breeders’ Cup Dirt Mile (GI) and his next start.


‘COOKIN’ WIT CAT’ – CATALANO’S GREATEST THANKSGIVING HITS – Trainer Wayne Catalano was headed home from Churchill Downs on Wednesday to get a head start on Thanksgiving dinner for his family with his oyster stuffing and baked macaroni and cheese back on the menu.


“I’m thankful for my family, especially my wife, Renee, and for the life we get to share,” Catalano said. “Horse racing is special to me but getting to spend time with my family is even better.”


Catalano first shared his oyster stuffing recipe in 2022. He cooks down carrots, celery and onions, browns seasoned ground chuck and soaks stale bread in the oyster juices. He mixes the oysters and soaked bread with the beef and vegetables before baking.


His baked macaroni and cheese takes its cue from Rocky & Carlo’s in Chalmette, La. He uses long macaroni and whatever cheeses he has on hand, melts the cheese on the stove and finishes the dish in the oven.


“On Thanksgiving, oven space is at a premium,” Catalano said. “If there’s too much going on in there, you can finish it on the grill – just close the lid until the cheese starts to bubble.”


This year, Catalano added a recipe for those shipping to Fair Grounds for the winter: New Orleans-style barbecue shrimp.


“I like to keep it pretty simple because you don’t need to do much with shrimp, they’re good as it is,” Catalano said


Catalano seasons shrimp with black pepper and bakes them in butter until just cooked through, about 35 minutes depending on the size of the shrimp and the batch. He serves them with a good loaf of French bread to soak up the juices. Catalano said some recipes may call for Worcestershire sauce but he prefers to keep it simple with just black pepper.


Outside of the kitchen, Catalano will wrap the holiday week Sunday at Churchill Downs where Eclipse Thoroughbred Partners’ multiple graded stakes winner Built is the 7-5 morning line choice in the $250,000 Cherokee Mile.


THANKSGIVING TRADITION, 10 STAKES CLOSE FALL MEET – Churchill Downs will serve about 7,500 turkey dinners on Thanksgiving Day and stage 10 stakes worth $3.4 million over the final five days of the 137th Fall Meet, highlighted by Friday’s $700,000 Clark (Grade II) and Saturday’s return of the Road to the Kentucky Derby.


First post is 1 p.m. (all times Eastern) except Thursday’s Thanksgiving Day card, which begins at 11:30 a.m.


Wednesday, Nov. 25
Brazilian Group 1 winner Night of Rose, beaten a neck at Keeneland in her last start, is entered in the featured $134,000 allowance optional claimer for fillies and mares at 1 1/8 miles on turf in Race 7 at 3:55 p.m.
The 20-cent Derby City 6 begins in Race 5 at 2:57 p.m. with a $75,710 carryover. The $1 Jackpot 8 has a $510,380 carryover and is scheduled for Race 10 at 5:25 p.m.
Thursday, Nov. 26
Churchill Downs first hosted a Thanksgiving Day program in 1928 but it wasn’t until 1969 that it became a Louisville tradition when the track opened Skye Terrace for individual or group dining reservations. Now, the region’s largest Thanksgiving dinner runs from 11 a.m. to 3 p.m. and includes a chef’s table menu of herb-roasted turkey, Kentucky smoked ham, stuffing, whipped potatoes and green bean casserole. Gates open at 10 a.m. and the last of 12 races goes at 4:43 p.m.
Levy Restaurants chefs will begin to cook the Thanksgiving meal around 1 a.m., and the menu consists of preparing approximately 550 10-pound turkeys, 6,000 pounds of spiral ham, 250 gallons of rosemary gravy, 5,000 pounds of mashed potatoes, 150 gallons of cranberry sauce and more than 900 pumpkin pies.
Juddmonte’s unbeaten Consequent seeks her fifth straight win in the $300,000 Falls City (Grade III), a Thanksgiving Day fixture since 1978. The 1 1/8-mile race goes as Race 11 at 4:14 p.m. Patricia Moseley’s Proctor Street defends her title in the $300,000 Cardinal presented by Resolute Racing (Listed), a 1 1/8-mile turf race scheduled as Race 9 at 3:16 p.m.
Friday, Nov. 27
Wathnan Racing’s unbeaten Travers winner Leading Change faces older horses in the 152nd running of the $700,000 Clark presented by Norton Healthcare (GII), the richest race of the 24-day Fall Meet. The 1 1/8-mile Clark goes as Race 11 at 5:54 p.m. Rigney Racing’s Tam Tam, a winner of back-to-back Grade I races, leads the $300,000 Mrs. Revere (GII) at 1 1/16 miles on turf in Race 10 at 5:25 p.m.
Qatar Racing’s $1.4 million Fasig-Tipton Saratoga Sale purchase Caesar, by Justify and a half-brother to 2022 Breeders’ Cup Turf Sprint winner Caravel, is scheduled to debut for trainer Brad Cox in a $120,000 maiden special weight at 5 ½ furlongs on turf in Race 5 at 2:55 p.m.
Thomas Bachman’s Kehoe Beach, the 2024 Mrs. Revere winner, faces open company an hour before this year’s running in a $148,000 turf sprint in Race 8 at 4:25 p.m. The Wesley Ward trainee was beaten a nose in the $400,000 Franklin (GII) at Keeneland last month.
Saturday, Nov. 28
The 12-race Stars of Tomorrow II program drew 141 2-year-olds, including 11 also-eligibles. Grade I-placed Coach Pope and Street Sense (GIII) runner-up Staunch lead the 100th running of the $400,000 Kentucky Jockey Club (GII) in Race 12 at 6:26 p.m. Rags to Riches winner Wharfie tops the $400,000 Fasig-Tipton Golden Rod (GII) in Race 10 at 5:25 p.m. The $225,000 Fern Creek (Listed) goes as Race 9 at 4:55 p.m. and the $225,000 Ed Brown as Race 11 at 5:54 p.m.
Saturday’s card includes six $120,000 maiden special weights and two $127,000 allowance optional claimers. Since Churchill Downs introduced Stars of Tomorrow in 2005, the programs have featured 103 Grade I or Group 1 winners, including four Kentucky Derby winners and eight Kentucky Oaks winners. Last year, Further Ado gave Cox his 500th Churchill Downs win when he scored a 1 ¾-length victory in the Kentucky Jockey Club. The colt went on to win the Breeders’ Cup Dirt Mile (GI) at Keeneland last month.
Cox and Steve Asmussen, who enter the week tied atop the trainer standings, send out a duo of colts who sold for a combined $4.8 million at the 2025 Fasig-Tipton Saratoga Sale in Saturday’s $127,000 one-mile allowance optional claimer in Race 7 at 3:55 p.m. Cox’s $3 million Into Mischief colt Lord Mischief won his debut at Stars of Tomorrow I on Oct. 25. Asmussen’s $1.8 million Flightline colt Powerline broke his maiden on the Breeders’ Cup undercard at Keeneland on Oct. 31.
Flying Dutchmen’s Let Love Reign, a $1 million Keeneland September Yearling Sale purchase by Not This Time, debuts for Brian Lynch in Race 3 at 1:56 p.m. Her dam, Road to Victory, handed Monomoy Girl her first of only three career defeats in the 2017 Golden Rod. Leland Ackerley Racing’s Dismantle, a $1 million Fasig-Tipton Midlantic May purchase from the first crop of champion Corniche, debuts for trainer Steve Asmussen in Race 6 at 3:25 p.m.
Sunday, Nov. 29
Dogwood (GIII) winner Conceit and Eight Belles (GII) winner Look Forward meet in the $300,000 Chilukki (GIII) in Race 11 at 5:54 p.m. Vanderbilt (GII) winner Built and Kentucky Derby (GI) fourth-place finisher Chief Wallabee are entered in the $250,000 Cherokee Mile in Race 10 at 5:25 p.m. The closing day card features mandatory payouts in all multi-race wagers, including the 20-cent Derby City 6, which starts in Race 7 at 3:55 p.m.
Reagan’s Honor makes his first start since the April 4 Blue Grass (GI) in a $134,000 allowance optional claimer that includes 2025 Peter Pan winner Hill Road in Race 4 at 2:24 p.m.
Four entrants in a $120,000 maiden special weight in Race 8 at 4:25 p.m. brought a combined $3,675,000 at auction. Juddmonte’s $1 million Tribal Governance debuts for Bill Mott against a field that includes Fun to Tap ($1.2 million), Colossus ($975,000) and Mojacar ($500,000), a half-brother to Test (GI) winner Kilwin.
ROAD TO THE KENTUCKY DERBY AND KENTUCKY OAKS
The Kentucky Jockey Club is the first U.S. Derby points race since the Oct. 30 Breeders’ Cup Juvenile. The Kentucky Jockey Club and Golden Rod will be run at 1 1/16 miles and award 10-5-3-2-1 points to the top five on the Derby and Oaks trails, respectively. The Japan Road to the Kentucky Derby opens on the same points scale in the 1,600-meter Cattleya Stakes on dirt at Tokyo Racecourse. Post time is 11:50 p.m. Saturday (1:50 p.m. Sunday in Japan).
KENTUCKY DERBY FUTURE WAGERS
Pool 2 of the Kentucky Derby Future Wager and the Kentucky Derby Sire Future Wager run from noon Thursday to 6 p.m. Sunday. Unbeaten Breeders’ Cup Juvenile winner Hughes is Pool 2’s 6-1 individual morning-line favorite, and “All Others Foaled in 2024” is the 2-1 overall choice. In the Sire Future Wager, Hughes’ sire Into Mischief is the 4-1 favorite and Gun Runner is the second choice at 6-1. Both pools offer $2 win and exacta wagering.
SIRE POWER DEBUTS SATURDAY
Eight Kentucky stallion farms will compete for a share of $80,000 in the inaugural Sire Power contest. In the golf-style skins format, eligible runners earn their sire’s farm 4-3-2-1 points for finishing first through fourth. Unclaimed points roll over to the same finishing position in the next race. Fans can follow the standings on the Big Board throughout the card. The participating farms are Airdrie Stud, Claiborne Farm, Coolmore America’s Ashford Stud, Hill ’n’ Dale Farms at Xalapa, Lane’s End, Spendthrift Farm, Taylor Made Stallions and WinStar Farm.
FALL MEET LEADERS
Luis Saez leads the jockey standings through 19 days with 27 wins, followed by apprentice Yomar Ortiz Jr. (20), Jose Ortiz (16), Tyler Gaffalione (15) and Walter Rodriguez (12).
Defending Fall Meet champion Brad Cox and Steve Asmussen share the trainer lead with 14 wins apiece. Joe Sharp is third with 12, followed by Eddie Kenneally (seven) and Kenny McPeek (six).
Godolphin leads the owner standings with six wins, one ahead of Asmussen. Epic Horses, Rigney Racing and Team Adams Racing share third with three wins apiece.
HOLIDAY SPIRIT
Santa and Mrs. Claus will meet guests in the second-floor Clubhouse Food Court from 4:15-5:30 p.m. Friday and 2:15-4:30 p.m. Saturday. Children can write letters to Santa and take part in holiday crafts. The final Stakes Room Brunch of the Fall Meet begins at noon Sunday.
